assignments.node_id: צמצומים רבים. מעלה לעלול, משכל עליון לשכל תחתון
assignments.reason: Many contractions (tzimtzumim rabbim) IS the essential mechanism of the lower intellect: the process by which the vast upper sekhel is compressed step-by-step into graspable form. The Torah opens with this as the defining description of how sekhel tachton works (line 7). Its essential nature is the cognitive-structural process of contraction — identical to the domain of Package 1 (malkhut = sekhel tachton = the concentrating lens).

Comprehension of Divinity is the ultimate goal of the sekhel elyon/tachton structure. The Torah opens: 'Hasagot Elokut is impossible except through many tzimtzumim, from upper to lower intellect' (line 7). Its essential nature is divine apprehension — the content that the cognitive structure of Package 1 is designed to make accessible. It IS what sekhel elyon contains and what sekhel tachton makes graspable.

Chokhmah (wisdom) in this Torah is the broader wisdom-domain that includes chokhmah tata'ah (already in Package 1). The proof text says 'through the rebuker's opening of the mouth, chokhmah is revealed' and 'the main revelation of chesed is through chokhmah, for El nehiru de-chakhmeta' (line 49). Its essential nature is wisdom/intellect — the same cognitive domain as Package 1, which already holds chokhmah tata'ah, chokhmah hamanheget, and the entire sekhel structure. It PRODUCES chesed (causal) but it IS wisdom (essential nature).

Chesed in this Torah is specifically the Abrahamic attribute that restores and elevates malkhut: 'vehukon bechesed kisei' — the throne (= malkhut) is established through chesed (line 40). Abraham was the man of chesed who 'tikken shacharit' (= sekhel tachton = malkhut, line 42) and pursued the four kings to redeem malkhut. Chesed's essential nature here is the activating/restoring quality of malkhut — it is misitra de-malkhut, the force that cuts malkhut free from exile. It belongs to the malkhut domain because the Torah defines chesed as malkhut's lifeline, not as a separate domain.

The revelation of chesed shares the same essential nature as chesed itself — it is chesed becoming active/manifest. The Torah says 'the main revelation of chesed — through which one cuts and separates the dalet (malkhut) from the four exiles — is through tokhachah' (line 49). Hitgalut hachesed is the actualization of malkhut's restoration mechanism, placing it in the malkhut domain of Package 1.

assignments.node_id: צריך לראות לחתך ולהבדיל את בחינות המלכות הנ"ל מבין הארבע גליות, ולהעלותה משם
assignments.reason: This node describes the imperative to cut and separate malkhut from the four exiles and elevate it. Its essential nature is entirely about malkhut — it IS the process of malkhut's redemption. The Torah (line 40) frames this as the central challenge: malkhut falls into the four exiles and must be extracted via chesed. This belongs in Package 1 as a direct expression of malkhut's dynamic.

assignments.node_id: שונא בצע, שישנא הממון בתכלית השנאה
assignments.reason: Hating money is the ethical prerequisite for attaining sekhel tachton. The Torah explicitly states: 'sonei betza is misitra de-malkhut' — hating money IS from the side of malkhut (line 25). When Samuel's generation fell into money-love, they damaged malkhut diqdushah; when Solomon's era valued silver as nothing, malkhut was restored (lines 26-27). Its essential nature is a quality OF the malkhut domain — not merely something that leads to it, but a manifestation of the same malkhut-side reality.

Tokhachah (rebuke) IS the defining action of the rebuking tzaddik. Package 3 already contains the rebuker's voice (qol hamokhi'ach), the horn of the shofar (qeren hashofar), and the tzaddik himself. Tokhachah is not merely something the tzaddik does — it IS his essential function in this Torah. The entire section 7 (line 49) defines the tzaddik's tokhachah as the mechanism through which wisdom and chesed are revealed. Its essential nature is the tzaddik's rebuke-function.

Receiving the Torah is enabled by azut diqdushah (line 59): 'Why was Torah given to Israel? Because they are brazen.' Package 3 already contains Torah haqedoshah and 'pesel lekha' — the holy Torah in its solid, weighty form. Qabbalat haTorah (receiving Torah) shares this essential nature: it IS the actualization of holy Torah through holy boldness. The tzaddik discerns whether a person has received genuine Torah or pesilim, making Torah-reception integral to the tzaddik's discernment domain.

Generic azut (boldness) is the quality the tzaddik perceives in each person to discern their spiritual state: 'through the azut that the tzaddik sees in each person — whether azut diqdushah or the opposite — he knows whether their prayer was proper' (line 63). Its essential nature is the raw quality of boldness that can tip either way (holy or evil). It belongs in Package 3 because it is the OBJECT of the tzaddik's discernment — the signal he reads. Polarity is neutral because generic azut encompasses both holy boldness and evil audacity; it is the tzaddik's task to distinguish them.

Prayer (singular tefillah) shares the essential nature of tefillot (plural, already in Package 3). The Torah says prayer requires azut — 'it is impossible to stand and pray before Hashem except through boldness' (line 63). Prayer is what Mashiach receives and discerns through his nose/smell. Tefillah is the individual instance of what tefillot describes collectively — the same essential nature of the prayer-domain in the tzaddik/Mashiach package.

The mitzvot's essential nature in this Torah is as the source of simcha that gathers into the festivals: 'the main simcha is from the mitzvot... and the simcha of all the mitzvot done throughout the year gathers into the heart, which is the three festivals' (lines 31-32). The mitzvot are not generic commandments here — they are specifically framed as the year-round feeders whose joy accumulates into the regalim. Their essential nature in Torah #30 is integral to the festival-cycle domain of Package 2.

Simcha (joy) IS the essential quality of the three festivals: 'therefore they are days of simcha — vesamachta bechagekha' (line 32). The Torah defines simcha as what accumulates in the heart (= regalim = binah = liba) and produces or-hapanim: 'lev same'ach yeitiv panim' (line 31). Simcha's essential nature is not a generic emotion but the specific spiritual light of the festival-time. It belongs in Package 2 as the defining quality of the regalim.
